blocks.content: Introduction to Housekeeping & clean work area discipline
Explain why clean work areas prevent safety and quality issues (FOD/accidents).

items.definition: Keeping walkways and work areas clutter-free in a Part 145 shop prevents FOD (Foreign Object Damage/Debris), trip hazards for personnel, and tool loss — all of which directly affect airworthiness and safety.
items.analogy: Like a hospital operating room floor — a dropped scalpel (or screw) creates both a personnel hazard and a risk of ending up somewhere it shouldn't.

blocks.question: Why is keeping walkways and work areas free of clutter critical in a Part 145 repair station?
choices: OSHA requires it primarily for general workplace aesthetics
It prevents FOD, trip hazards, and tool loss that could affect airworthiness and personnel safety
Clutter causes EMI interference with avionics test equipment calibration
It is only required during FAA surveillance visits and scheduled audits
blocks.feedback: Clutter in an avionics shop creates three key risks: FOD (hardware, wire scraps, or tools entering aircraft systems), trip and fall hazards, and tool accountability failures. All three directly impact safety and airworthiness.
